 GAO Finds Gaps in CMS Medicare Fraud Risk Assessments, With 21 of 31 Areas Not Yet Started
 November 18, 2026 
 A new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report identifies gaps in how the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) assesses and manages fraud risks in traditional Medicare, including unfinished risk assessments, shortcomings in evaluating existing fraud controls, and limited coordination with HHS.
 According to the November 18 report, CMS’s Center for Program Integrity (CPI) had started risk assessments for 10 of 31 identified Medicare topic areas since 2022. As of July 2026, CMS could not provide GAO evidence that any of those assessments or 28 related vulnerability summaries had been completed.
 GAO also found that CPI’s vulnerability management process does not systematically assess the likelihood and impact of specific fraud risks or examine whether existing antifraud controls are effective. The review identified additional risks involving durable medical equipment suppliers, provider enrollment screening, and potentially fraudulent billing that were not fully addressed in CMS’s assessments.
 The findings involve a program that reported nearly $481 billion in Medicare Fee-for-Service benefit spending in 2025. CMS currently uses its Fraud Prevention System, data analytics, and Unified Program Integrity Contractors (UPICs) to identify potentially fraudulent claims and investigate suspected fraud.
 GAO made four recommendations addressing risk assessments, documentation, coordination with HHS, and fraud risk management procedures. HHS agreed with three but disputed the recommendation to revise CMS’s vulnerability management process, maintaining that its existing approach already addresses Medicare fraud risks. GAO disagreed.
 The report reflects work conducted between March and November 2026, with several findings based on information available as of July. HHS also described ongoing fraud prevention initiatives, including enhanced oversight and restrictions on certain durable medical equipment supplier enrollments.
 Read the full GAO report, Medicare: HHS and CMS Should Better Manage Fraud Risks (GAO-27-109072).
